facts.raw_span: A man in his 60s presented with a 3-month history of intertrigo involving his groin
he had been treating with a combination of clotrimazole cream, 1%, and hydrocortisone cream, 1%
bright red, burning and painful nodules around his scrotum
Two symmetrical solitary erythematous nodules were present in the right and left inguinal folds adjacent to the scrotum
Epidermal ulceration overlying a diffuse dermal proliferation composed of sheets of histiocytes with eosinophilic granular cytoplasm
Intracytoplasmic Michaelis-Gutmann bodies present as basophilic, somewhat laminated intracytoplasmic inclusion bodies measuring 5-8 μm in diameter
Bodies highlighted with iron (Prussian blue) and calcium (Von Kossa) stains
Background population of many plasma cells and few neutrophils noted
Fungus culture: Negative
Atypical mycobacteria culture: Negative
Bacterial culture: Positive for E. coli
Medical history included prostate cancer, hypertension, anxiety disorder, hyperlipidemia, gastroesophageal reflux disease, and diverticulosis

concepts.why: The presence of Michaelis-Gutmann bodies and the histopathological examination results are characteristic of Malakoplakia.
The positive bacterial culture for E. coli suggests an E. coli infection.
The presence of calcium deposits and the histopathological examination results are characteristic of Calcinosis.
The presence of plasma cells and neutrophils suggests a chronic inflammatory disease.
The presence of erythematous nodules and the histopathological examination results are characteristic of cutaneous malakoplakia.
The presence of histiocytes and plasma cells suggests a granulomatous disease.

rationales.F03: Bright red, burning, and painful nodules are consistent with malakoplakia and cutaneous malakoplakia.
rationales.F05: Epidermal ulceration and diffuse dermal proliferation with histiocytes are characteristic of malakoplakia and cutaneous malakoplakia.
rationales.F06: Intracytoplasmic Michaelis-Gutmann bodies are pathognomonic for malakoplakia and cutaneous malakoplakia.
rationales.F07: The presence of iron and calcium stains highlights the Michaelis-Gutmann bodies, supporting malakoplakia and calcinosis.
rationales.F08: The background population of plasma cells and neutrophils is consistent with malakoplakia, cutaneous malakoplakia, and chronic inflammatory disease.
rationales.F11: The positive bacterial culture for E. coli suggests an E. coli infection, but the presence of Michaelis-Gutmann bodies and other histopathological features rule out a simple E. coli infection.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of Michaelis-Gutmann bodies and the histopathological examination findings are highly specific for malakoplakia, and the cutaneous presentation matches Cutaneous malakoplakia.
